## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Curves shapes
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Plane arcs, function graphs, and polynomial pieces
//  - Polar and figure curves in 2D
//  - Plane spirals, transition curves, and roulettes
//  - Analytic curves in 3D

//==
// # Plane arcs, function graphs, and polynomial pieces
//
// The elementary open pieces of plane geometry: conic arcs, the graphs of the
// standard transcendental functions, and the quadratic and cubic Bezier arcs
// that vector graphics is built from. Each type stores the minimal defining
// parameters; the canonical [0,1] curve parameter maps onto the documented
// sweep or domain. Types whose placement fields are absent are defined in
// canonical position (centered at or starting from the origin) and are placed
// elsewhere with a transform. Evaluation lives in
// `curves-shapes.library.plato`.

//==
// # Arcs and conic pieces

// A portion of a circle: the points at distance Radius from Center, swept over
// the angle interval measured from the +X axis
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circular_arc).
type CircularArc2D
    implements ICurve2D
{
    Center: Point2D;
    Radius: Number;
    Angles: AngleInterval;
}

// A portion of an axis-rotated ellipse. Radii holds the semi-axis lengths along
// the ellipse's local X and Y; Rotation tilts the major frame from the +X axis;
// Angles sweeps the parametric angle (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellipse).
type EllipticalArc2D
    implements ICurve2D
{
    Center: Point2D;
    Radii: Number2;
    Rotation: Angle;
    Angles: AngleInterval;
}

// A parabola in canonical position: y = Coefficient * x * x, vertex at the
// origin, opening along +Y. The parameter is x, ranging over Domain
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parabola).
type Parabola2D
    implements ICurve2D
{
    Coefficient: Number;
    Domain: NumberInterval;
}

//==
// # Function graphs

// The graph of a hanging chain: y = Scale * cosh(x / Scale). Scale is the
// classic catenary constant a; the parameter is x, ranging over Domain
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catenary).
type Catenary2D
    implements ICurve2D
{
    Scale: Number;
    Domain: NumberInterval;
}

// One or more cycles of a sine wave along the X axis:
// y = Amplitude * sin(2 * pi * x / Wavelength + Phase). The parameter is x,
// ranging over Domain (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sine_wave).
type SineCurve2D
    implements ICurve2D
{
    Amplitude: Number;
    Wavelength: Number;
    Phase: Angle;
    Domain: NumberInterval;
}

//==
// # Polynomial arcs

// A quadratic Bezier arc: interpolates P0 to P2, shaped by the middle control
// point P1. Tangents at the ends aim at P1
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9zier_curve).
type QuadraticBezier2D
    implements ICurve2D, IDeformable2D
{
    P0: Point2D;
    P1: Point2D;
    P2: Point2D;
}

// A cubic Bezier arc: interpolates P0 to P3, shaped by the interior control
// points P1 and P2. The workhorse of vector graphics and font outlines
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9zier_curve).
type CubicBezier2D
    implements ICurve2D, IDeformable2D
{
    P0: Point2D;
    P1: Point2D;
    P2: Point2D;
    P3: Point2D;
}

//==
// # Polar and figure curves in 2D
//
// The named plane curves whose natural description is a radius as a function of
// angle — roses, cardioids, limacons, lemniscates, and the classical trisecting
// and conchoidal cubics — together with the two figure curves (Lissajous,
// butterfly) that are drawn the same way. Most are `IPolarCurve2D`, so a single
// RadiusAt body is their whole implementation; those live in
// `curves-shapes.library.plato`. Every type is in canonical position about
// the origin and is placed elsewhere with a transform.

//==
// # Polar and figure curves

// The rose r = Radius * cos(PetalFrequency * theta). A whole odd frequency k
// yields k petals; a whole even k yields 2k petals; fractional frequencies
// close only over multiple turns
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_(mathematics)).
type RoseCurve2D
    implements IPolarCurve2D
{
    Radius: Number;
    PetalFrequency: Number;
}

// The cardioid r = 2 * Radius * (1 + cos theta): the heart-shaped path traced
// by a circle of radius Radius rolling around an equal fixed circle. Always
// closed; total width is 4 * Radius (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardioid).
type Cardioid2D
    implements IClosedCurve2D
{
    Radius: Number;
}

// The limacon r = Offset + Amplitude * cos theta. Offset > Amplitude gives a
// dimpled oval, equality gives the cardioid, Offset < Amplitude adds an inner
// loop. Always closed (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lima%C3%A7on).
type Limacon2D
    implements IClosedCurve2D
{
    Offset: Number;
    Amplitude: Number;
}

// The lemniscate of Bernoulli, r * r = Scale * Scale * cos(2 * theta): a
// figure-eight crossing itself at the origin; Scale is the half-width
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lemniscate_of_Bernoulli).
type Lemniscate2D
    implements IClosedCurve2D
{
    Scale: Number;
}
```
